_comment: Scripted session transcripts for the knowledge-pipeline benchmark. Each session carries planted ground truth: `expected` facts the distiller MUST extract (gist matched by an LLM judge; `intent:true` marks the user-context channel the v1 prompt systematically missed) and `forbidden` items it MUST NOT extract. Event shapes mirror what the runtime persists (see orchestrator/src/memory/slim.ts).

data.text: for the merchant plugins, we will NOT use a central marketplace. the reason is that every merchant self-hosts the admin panel on their own VPS, there is no central acme server to serve a marketplace from. generate install artifacts per-instance at setup time instead. i also considered a shared registry with signed bundles and rejected it - it recreates the central server we are avoiding.

content.text: Understood — per-instance artifact generation it is. I've built the installer to emit artifacts parameterized with the instance URL and per-merchant token at setup time. No registry, no central fetch; each admin panel serves its own artifacts.
Done. The setup flow now writes the plugin bundle with the instance URL baked in; tests pass.

expected.gist: Merchant plugins are distributed WITHOUT a central marketplace: install artifacts are generated per-instance at setup time, because every merchant self-hosts the admin panel on their own VPS and there is no central server. A shared signed-bundle registry was considered and rejected for recreating the central server.

forbidden.gist: The installer was built / the session shipped the artifact generator / tests pass

data.text: you keep verifying by curling endpoints. that is not verification. always test like a real merchant would: create a store, add a product, go through the whole checkout as a shopper, see the money move in the sandbox. mimic the consumer journey end to end, every time.

content.text: Point taken — I ran the full journey: created a fresh store, added a product, checked out as a shopper, and confirmed the sandbox charge appeared. The tax line was correct this time.

expected.gist: Verification must be done as a real merchant/shopper journey end to end (create store, add product, complete checkout, see sandbox charge) — not by curling endpoints.

forbidden.gist: The tax line was correct in this session's run

data.text: the webhook worker keeps crashing on boot in staging, logs attached. figure it out
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'signingSecret') at WebhookVerifier.init (src/webhooks/verify.ts:41) — env WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET unset in staging

content.text: Root cause found and fixed: WebhookVerifier.init dereferences config.signingSecret unconditionally, so a missing WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET env crashes the worker at boot instead of failing one verification. Staging never had the secret set. I added a boot-time guard that fails fast with a clear message naming the missing env var, and set the secret in staging. Worker boots clean now.

expected.gist: A missing WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET env var crashes the webhook worker at boot (TypeError reading 'signingSecret' in WebhookVerifier.init / src/webhooks/verify.ts) rather than failing a single verification.

data.text: how does the tax calculation work for EU orders?

content.text: EU orders flow through TaxResolver.forRegion('eu') which applies the destination country's VAT rate from the rates table, with the reverse-charge path for B2B orders carrying a validated VAT ID. The rates table refreshes weekly from the upstream feed. Nothing here is custom per merchant.

forbidden.gist: EU orders use TaxResolver / VAT rates / reverse charge (any restatement of the explained mechanics as a memory)

data.text: shoppers on mobile safari report their carts vanish after a few minutes. find out why

content.text: First hypothesis: Redis eviction dropping cart keys under memory pressure. Checking eviction stats and TTLs now.

Redis is exonerated — zero evictions, cart keys alive with correct TTLs while a reporter's cart was already 'gone'. The real cause: the session cookie is set with Domain=www.acme-checkout.com, and mobile Safari opens the apple-pay return flow on acme-checkout.com without the www — no cookie, fresh anonymous session, cart looks empty. Fix shipped: cookie Domain=.acme-checkout.com (leading dot), verified on a device — cart survives the return flow now.

expected.gist: Mobile-Safari cart loss was caused by the session cookie being scoped to www.acme-checkout.com while the Apple Pay return flow lands on the bare domain — fixed by setting cookie Domain=.acme-checkout.com. (Redis eviction was investigated and ruled out.)

forbidden.gist: Redis eviction under memory pressure causes cart loss (the ruled-out hypothesis stated as fact)

data.text: the build box is out of disk, clean it up

content.text: Permission denied by policy: destructive command requires explicit approval
The policy layer blocked docker system prune. I freed 9GB instead by clearing the npm cache and removing dangling build artifacts under /tmp/builds older than 7 days. Disk is at 61% now.

forbidden.gist: The user has a rule/preference against docker system prune or destructive docker commands

data.text: do we retry failed payment webhooks? a merchant asked

content.text: Yes — confirmed in src/webhooks/dispatch.ts: failed deliveries retry 5 times with exponential backoff starting at 30s and doubling (30s, 1m, 2m, 4m, 8m), then land in the dead_letters table for manual replay. I've verified the dead-letter path with a forced failure.

expected.gist: Failed payment webhook deliveries retry 5 times with exponential backoff starting at 30 seconds (doubling each attempt), then go to the dead_letters table for manual replay (src/webhooks/dispatch.ts).

data.text: merchant says they got the same webhook 6 times, is that a bug?

content.text: Not a bug — their endpoint was returning 500s, and our dispatcher retries failed webhook deliveries up to five times with exponential backoff (first retry after 30 seconds, doubling), before dead-lettering. Six deliveries = the original plus five retries. Their fix is to return 200 on duplicate receipt; ours is nothing.

expected.gist: Webhook deliveries that fail are retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff (first retry 30s, doubling) before dead-lettering.

data.text: heads up: staging now sends REAL email through Postmark since yesterday. the old mailhog capture is gone. be careful with test orders using real addresses

content.text: Noted — staging email goes out for real via Postmark now; Mailhog capture is gone. I'll use @example.test addresses for test orders so nothing real receives mail.

preseed_memory.claim: Staging never sends real email: all outbound mail on staging is captured by Mailhog and no external SMTP is configured.

expected.gist: Staging sends real email via Postmark (the Mailhog capture was removed), so test orders must use non-real addresses.

data.text: set up the payment env for the new deploy target. key is sk-live-BENCH-FAKE-KEY-000001, keep it out of the repo obviously

content.text: Configured — the deploy target reads STRIPE_SECRET_KEY from the environment store; nothing landed in the repo. Deploys fail fast with a named error when the variable is missing.

expected.gist: The deploy target requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in the environment store; deploys fail fast with a named error when it is missing.

forbidden.gist: Any claim containing the literal secret key value sk-live-BENCH

data.text: for now refunds stay manual through support. but next quarter i want shoppers to self-serve refunds from the order portal, within a merchant-set window. build nothing yet, just keep it in mind while designing the order model

content.text: Understood — refunds stay manual for now. I've kept the order state machine open for a shopper-initiated refund transition later (states are data-driven, no code change needed to add one), and noted the merchant-set refund window as a future merchant setting.

expected.gist: Committed future intention: shoppers will self-serve refunds from the order portal within a merchant-set window (targeted next quarter); refunds stay manual through support until then.

data.text: the bar for onboarding: a new merchant goes from signup to their first successful checkout in under ten minutes, with exactly one command on their server. every onboarding decision gets measured against that sentence. if a step doesn't serve it, kill the step

content.text: That's a crisp bar. Auditing the current flow against it: the DNS verification step and the manual webhook URL paste both fail the test — I've folded DNS verification into the install command and auto-registered the webhook URL. Signup-to-first-checkout is now 4 steps.

expected.gist: The onboarding north star: a new merchant goes from signup to first successful checkout in under ten minutes with exactly one command on their server — every onboarding decision is measured against this.

forbidden.gist: The flow is now 4 steps / DNS verification was folded in this session
